sections.label: Motion on independent Speaker
sections.summary: The Motion concerns the desirability of an independent, impartial Speaker and a fair Parliament, not the former Speaker's conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The subject matter of the Motion is on the general desirability for an independent and impartial Speaker and for Parliament to be a fair arena.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: This Motion is not a debate on the conduct of former Speaker Tan Chuan-Jin.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: In their speeches, Members should not impute improper motives to any other Member and, most specifically, rulings made by the former Speaker on any point of order cannot be reviewed by Parliament except upon a substantive Motion directly addressing those specific Points of Order.

sections.label: PSP on former Speaker conduct
sections.summary: The PSP believes the former Speaker's conduct brought Parliament into disrepute and deserves a full debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Even though Speaker Tan Chuan-Jin has resigned and apologised for his comment for Assoc Prof Jamus Lim's speech on the President's Address during the Parliamentary Sitting on 17 April 2023, the PSP believes that the conduct of the former Speaker has brought Parliament into disrepute and is a matter that deserves a full debate in this House.

sections.label: Standing Orders on speeches
sections.summary: The Speaker cites Standing Orders 50(1) and 50(6) and repeats that the Motion is not about the former Speaker's conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Well, I will get the exact Standing Order to you, but here, this Motion, I would like to repeat myself, in my opening remarks, it is not a debate on the conduct of former Speaker Tan Chuan-Jin.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: It is about – let me read your Motion, "That this House reaffirms its commitment to the need for the Speaker of Parliament to be independent and impartial and for Parliament to be a fair arena for all." That is your Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Leong, since you asked me which section of the Standing Order, Standing Order 50(1) states the content of speeches and this is why I say that Members, I reminded Members that they should confine their observations to the subject of the Motion to be discussed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: And in Standing Order 50(6), it states that in their speeches, Members should not impute improper motives to any other Member; and more specifically, I again repeated myself to say that rulings made by the former Speaker on any Point of Order cannot be reviewed by Parliament except upon a substantive Motion directly addressing those specific Points of Order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: If you would like a copy of the Standing Order, I can pass the book to you?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Hence, we are disappointed with the Prime Minister's confirmation during the Ministerial Statement just now that he would not have asked Speaker Tan to resign for his inappropriate comment.

sections.label: Speaker as PAP CEC member
sections.summary: It is difficult for the public to be convinced a ruling party core member can be impartial, so the Speaker should not be a PAP CEC member.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: It is also difficult for the public, especially those who do not support the ruling party, to be fully convinced that a core member of the ruling party can be an impartial presiding officer of the Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: We are of the view that the Speaker should at least not be a CEC member of the PAP.

sections.label: Non-partisan Speaker in future
sections.summary: As democracy develops and alternative and opposition MPs increase, the hope is for a non-partisan Speaker again, like AP Rajah in 1964.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: As our democracy develops and the number of alternative and opposition MPs, we hope the Speaker will be a non-partisan person again in the future, just like AP Rajah in 1964.

sections.label: Restoring confidence in Speaker
sections.summary: The House and new Speaker must restore public confidence in the Speaker's independence and impartiality, and Members should support the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: There is much work to be done by this House and our new Speaker to restore public confidence in the independence and impartiality of the office of Speaker, which has taken a body blow by recent events.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: I call on Members to support the Motion tabled by Ms Hazel Poa and I, and unanimously reaffirm our commitment for the need for the Speaker of Parliament to be independent and impartial, and for Parliament to be a fair arena for all.

sections.label: Speaker needs majority support
sections.summary: The Speaker must command the support of the majority in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The most important point is the Speaker has to command the support of the majority in Parliament.

sections.label: First Speaker appointed 1955
sections.summary: Before independence, the first Speaker, Sir George Oehlers, was appointed by the Governor-General in 1955.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Before Singapore’s independence, when we had a Legislative Assembly under British Rule, the first Speaker, Sir George Oehlers, was appointed by the Governor-General, who was the representative of the Crown, and this was in 1955.

sections.label: Later Speakers not ruling party
sections.summary: Mr AP Rajah and Mr Punch Coomaraswamy were not from the ruling party but were nominated by the Prime Minister and endorsed by the majority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The next Speakers after him, Mr AP Rajah and Mr Punch Coomaraswamy, were not members of the ruling party but they were nominated by the Prime Minister and endorsed by the majority of the House.

sections.label: Speaker's duty and independence
sections.summary: The Speaker must ensure observance of Standing Orders and be independent and impartial, with checks on his conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Speaker has the duty to ensure observance of the Standing Orders by Members in Parliamentary proceedings and must be independent and impartial in doing so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our process also has its checks on the Speaker's conduct should the Speaker fail to discharge his duties properly.

sections.label: Three checks on Speaker
sections.summary: The Speaker has three sets of checks: his party, Parliament itself, and the ballot box.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Whereas under our system, as I mentioned, the Speaker has three sets of checks: the party he is from, the Parliament itself, and third, the ballot box.

sections.label: Party membership and independence
sections.summary: The Speaker being from a political party does not automatically mean he lacks independence in his duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Yet, despite the Speaker being from a political party and exercising these powers, nobody has seriously suggested the Australian Parliament is not a fair arena for debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I therefore do not think that the fact that the Speaker happens to be from a political party or from its leadership automatically means that he lacks independence in the performance of his duties as Speaker.

sections.label: Proposed amendment to Motion
sections.summary: The speaker asks permission to propose an amendment to the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, Mr Speaker, with your permission, may I propose an amendment to the Motion?

sections.label: Amendments on Speaker independence
sections.summary: Two amendments change the words on independence and add a duty to uphold the Standing Orders and the Parliament Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Two, "In line 2, to delete the words 'be independent and impartial' and to insert 'discharge his duties independently and impartially'; and Three, "At the end of line 2, to add 'and (b) to uphold the Standing Orders of Parliament and the obligations under the Parliament (Privileges, Immunities and Powers) Act 1962'".

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The amendments have been marked up in the handout for Members' reference.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: I agree with the PSP that the Speaker must act independently in the discharge of his duties.

sections.label: Rules in Standing Orders
sections.summary: Rules ensuring Parliament is a fair arena are in the Standing Orders and the Parliament Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: As I had explained earlier, many of the rules that ensure Parliament is a fair arena, including the rights and obligations that Members have, are all actually in the Standing Orders and the Parliament (Privileges, Immunities and Powers) Act.

sections.label: Three amendments to Motion
sections.summary: Three amendments are stated, and the speaker asks Members' agreement, noting a former Speaker's off-the-cuff remark.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: First, "In line 1, after the word 'commitment', to insert '(a)'." Second, "In line 2, to delete 'be independent and impartial' and to insert 'discharge his duties independently and impartially'." And the third amendment is, "At the end of line 2, to add 'and (b) to uphold the Standing Orders of Parliament and the obligations under the Parliament (Privileges, Immunities and Powers) Act 1962'".

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Do I have the hon Members' agreement to this?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I am also keenly aware that possibly, one of the catalysts for this Motion – on the need for an independent and impartial Speaker – was because of an off-the-cuff remark made by the former Speaker on a speech that I had delivered in response to the President's Address to begin this House's second session.

sections.label: Debate on trade-offs
sections.summary: Matters involving trade-offs and redistribution cannot be resolved without genuine, passionate and animated debate with Parliamentary decorum.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Or tricky matters of individual liberty and socio-cultural norms, such as the debate over the repeal of 377A and the relative freedom of the media to publish their opinions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These examples are all fundamentally ones that involve trade-offs and redistribution, rather than efficiency and optimisation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: When that is the case, I believe it is impossible to successfully identify the right way forward for the society, unless there is genuine, passionate, and, dare I say, animated debate, with proper respect for Parliamentary decorum, of course.

sections.label: Evidence-based policy proposals
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will not dismiss alternative evidence-based policy proposals but offer evidence-based counterarguments.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: More generally, I am hopeful that this Government will not casually dismiss alternative, evidence-based policy proposals, put up in good faith, but offer equally evidence-based counterarguments when rejecting any given policy proposal.

sections.label: Constitution on Speaker and MP seats
sections.summary: Article 40(2) allows the Speaker to be elected from non-Minister MPs or non-MPs, and article 46(2)(b) vacates a seat on leaving one's party.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Article 40(2) of the Constitution provides that the Speaker of Parliament may be elected from amongst MPs who are not Ministers or Parliamentary Secretaries or from amongst persons who are not MPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Furthermore, article 46(2)(b) of the Constitution also provides that an MP's seat will fall vacant if he ceases to be a member of, is expelled or resigns from, the political party for which he stood in the election.

sections.label: Speakers elected from ruling party
sections.summary: All Speakers since then have been elected MPs from the ruling party.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: All Speakers since then, as mentioned by both Mr Leong and Mr Nair, have been elected MPs from the ruling party.

sections.label: Singapore versus UK Speaker system
sections.summary: Singapore's system differs from the UK's, where the Speaker severs ties with his former political party to be completely non-partisan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As mentioned by hon Member Nair, our Singapore system is different from the UK system, where the Speaker, upon his election, severs ties with his former political party so that he is, in all aspects of the job, a completely non-partisan figure.

sections.label: UK continuity principle for Speaker
sections.summary: The UK Parliament abides by a continuity principle, re-electing an incumbent Speaker after a general election even if the governing party changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The UK Parliament also abides by what is known as the "continuity principle", where an incumbent Speaker after being re-elected in a general election, would be re-elected as Speaker even if there was a change of the party forming the government.

sections.label: Karnataka Speaker resignation case
sections.summary: In Shrimanth Balasaheb Patil vs Hon Speaker of Karnataka, the court faced petitions of five Karnataka State parliament members against the Speaker, who refused their resignations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the case Shrimanth Balasaheb Patil vs Hon Speaker of Karnataka, the court was faced with the petitions of five members of the Karnataka State parliament against the Speaker of that house, who had refused to accept their resignations.

sections.label: Motion on Speaker's independence
sections.summary: The Member says the House cannot affirm a Motion inconsistent with the Constitution, but supports Mr Nair's amendment that the Speaker discharge duties independently and impartially.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Procedurally, I do not think that this House can affirm a Motion that is inconsistent with the Constitution or that would purport to constrain the provisions of the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I will, however, support the Motion as amended by hon Member Nair as it addresses my concerns that we do not inadvertently affirm that a Speaker be politically independent, meaning not being part of a political party, but instead, that he should discharge his duties independently and impartially which is indeed what we should expect of the Speaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It may seem a small change but Mr Nair's amendment changes the meaning of the Motion and removes doubt as to what exactly Parliament is affirming.

sections.label: Leong Mun Wai conduct apology
sections.summary: The Leader of the House said Mr Leong Mun Wai made wrong statements and was disrespectful, he apologised, and the Speaker concurred no further action was needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In April 2023, the Leader of the House raised the point that Mr Leong Mun Wai had made several statements in and out of Chamber which were wrong and not proper.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: She said that Mr Leong had addressed Speaker in a manner that was disrespectful, disregarded the authority of the Chair, and that drew a caution from her on the need to maintain proper demeanour in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: She said Mr Leong apologised to the Speaker in Chambers very shortly and clarified he had not intended to cast aspersions on the Ministers and admitted he was wrong to make the suggestions in his statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Leader of the House then said there was no need to take further action on this matter and she sought Mr Speaker's concurrence on this matter, in particular to the fact of disregarding the authority of the Chair is a matter for the Speaker, and then Mr Tan Chuan-Jin, as Speaker, said he concurred.

sections.label: Views on populist speeches
sections.summary: The speaker says it is impossible for anyone except a robot not to form views on whether a speech is populist, so he cannot support Mr Leong Mun Wai's Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In fact, I would submit it is impossible for anyone, except a robot, not to form their own views as to whether a speech is populist or not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, for that reason, I cannot support the Motion of Mr Leong Mun Wai and I would support the amended Motion as moved by Mr Vikram Nair.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Motion moved by Mr Leong Mun Wai is that "This House reaffirms its commitment to the need for the Speaker of Parliament to be independent and impartial and for Parliament to be a fair arena for all".

sections.label: Speaker fair and impartial
sections.summary: The speaker agrees a Speaker needs to be fair, impartial and independent, so he can agree with the first part of Mr Vikram Nair's amendment.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: But I do agree that a Speaker needs to be fair, impartial and to act independently.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: So, for that reason I would be able to agree with the first part of the amendment which Mr Vikram Nair has moved, which is that "This House affirms its commitment to the need for the Speaker of Parliament to discharge his duties independently and impartially".

sections.label: Standing Orders and privileges obligations
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with the second part of Mr Vikram Nair's amendment affirming commitment to the Standing Orders and the Parliament (Privileges, Immunities and Powers) Act.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Hence, we have the Standing Orders, which are supposed to govern the conduct of Members vis-à-vis one another, and also, the Parliament (Privileges, Immunities and Powers) Act which sets out what Members should and should not do, and what it means when you have privileges as an MP, how you should act and not abuse them.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: And, therefore, I agree with the second part of the amendment moved by Mr Vikram Nair, which is that "This House should also affirm its commitment to uphold the Standing Orders of Parliament and the obligations under the Parliament (Privileges, Immunities and Powers) Act", and if we all conducted ourselves accordingly, you would have a fair arena for all.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In this regard, before I go on to explain why I support the amended Motion, may I just clarify with Assoc Prof Jamus Lim because I heard him say that he supported the Motion, but I was not sure whether he meant the original Motion or whether he meant the amended Motion?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I support the original Motion and I will also support the amended Motion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The major Commonwealth democracies all recognise the need for the person holding the role of Speaker to act in an impartial manner when discharging his or her duties, and Singapore is no different.

sections.label: Speaker eligibility requirements
sections.summary: The speaker says any person meeting the eligibility requirements can be elected Speaker, so PSP's proposal for an independent Speaker is more limiting than Constitutional requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Thus, under our law, any person who meets these eligibility requirements can be elected as the Speaker.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, PSP's proposal to require a Speaker to be independent in the sense of not being a member of a political party or not being an MP is actually not in accordance with and much more limiting than the Constitutional requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Actually, you will find that in most of the major Westminster-style democracies like ours, the Speaker comes from the majority party.

sections.label: UK Speaker party convention
sections.summary: The UK has a convention where the Speaker resigns from his or her political party upon being appointed as Speaker.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The UK, for example, has a convention where the Speaker resigns from his or her political party upon being appointed as Speaker.

sections.label: Speaker's conduct and duties
sections.summary: It depends on how the individual holding the office of Speaker conducts himself or herself, and the Speaker must be mindful of the office's duties and obligations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: At the end of the day, it boils down to how the individual holding the office of Speaker conducts himself or herself, and it is very important that the Speaker is mindful of the duties and obligations that come with the office.

sections.label: Previous Speakers earned praise
sections.summary: Previous Speakers of Parliament in Singapore earned praise and respect from both sides of the House, even though they were members of a political party.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Previous Speakers of Parliament in Singapore have earned praise and respect from both sides of the House, even though they were a member of a political party.

sections.label: Praise for previous Speakers
sections.summary: The House approved, and Mr Low Thia Khiang said Mr Tan Soo Khoon won his respect for being fair and he did not feel discriminated against.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: You have the approval of the whole House.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I would also like to say a word of thanks to the previous Speaker who had a very good rapport with the Opposition." And also, speaking when Mr Tan Soo Khoon ended his appointment as Speaker in 2002 after 13 years in that role, Mr Low Thia Khiang from the WP rose to record his views as follows, "Mr Tan Soo Khoon, as Speaker of the House, has won my respect for being fair most of the time, if not all the time" and that "Being a non-PAP Member, I have not felt discriminated and I think this is important as he was the Speaker." So, that Mr Speaker, concludes the essential premise, which I am making – which is at the end of the day, it is about the individual how he or she conducts themselves and about making sure that all of us do our part in Parliament.

sections.label: Speaker and ruling party committee
sections.summary: They brought out historical examples and proposed that the Government ensure the Speaker does not belong to the ruling party's central committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: As a result, we brought out the historical examples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: And at the same time, we had just proposed that for the time being, Government, please ensure that the Speaker does not belong to the central committee of the ruling party.

sections.label: Seven recommendations for fairer Parliament
sections.summary: In his Adjournment Motion he put up seven recommendations, including bigger research budgets, more flexible timekeeping, and alternative-party MPs chairing committees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: In order to promote the debate, as I have said, more debate, I have put up seven recommendations in my Adjournment Motion making Parliament a fairer arena for all at the May Sitting this year, including bigger research budgets for MPs from alternative parties, more flexible timekeeping during clarifications and debates, and appointing MPs from alternative parties to chair the Public Accounts and Public Petitions Committees.

sections.label: One-third alternative MPs solution
sections.summary: The best solution is to have at least one-third or 33% alternative MPs, commensurate with the percentage of votes alternative parties have won.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Ultimately, the best solution to making our Parliament a fairer arena for all is to have at least one-third or 33% alternative MPs in this House, commensurate with the percentage of votes that alternative parties have already won among Singaporeans.

sections.label: Speakers of Parliament non-partisan
sections.summary: All Speakers of Parliament were non-partisan except for a brief period between 1963 and 1964 when Mr EW Barker was Speaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Except for a brief period between 1963 and 1964 when Mr EW Barker was Speaker of Parliament, all the Speakers of Parliament were non-partisan.

sections.label: PSP urges Speaker not PAP CEC
sections.summary: The PSP says being Speaker and a PAP CEC member is contradictory and urges the Speaker should at least not be a PAP CEC member.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The evolution, from having a non-partisan Speaker to a backbencher Speaker to Speakers who were ex-office holders or members of the PAP’s CEC, has caused many Singaporeans to question the independence and impartiality of the Speaker’s office over the past 50 plus years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The Progress Singapore Party (PSP) believes that being simultaneously the Speaker and a CEC member of the ruling party is contradictory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Hence, we urge that the Speaker should at least not be a CEC member of the PAP.

sections.label: Recording dissent on amendments
sections.summary: The Speaker puts three amendments by Mr Vikram Nair to the House and records the dissent of Mr Leong and Ms Hazel Poa.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We have now come to the conclusion of the debate and I shall put the questions to the House for decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We have three amendments proposed by Mr Vikram Nair.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Does any Member wishes for his dissent or abstention to be recorded or to claim a division before I declare the result?

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Alright, we will have it recorded that Mr Leong and Ms Hazel Poa want their dissent recorded.
